question: What are the 'Four Last Things' in traditional Catholic eschatology?

choices.C: Purgatory, Heaven, Hell, and the Rapture
choices.D: Baptism, Confirmation, Last Rites, and Heaven

teaching.title: The Four Last Things
teaching.body: The traditional Catholic schema of the Four Last Things (Death, Judgment, Heaven, Hell) derives from Sirach 7:36: 'In whatever you do, remember your last days.' They form a classic framework for spiritual reflection. Death is universal and marks the end of earthly life and merit. Judgment follows immediately (Particular Judgment) and finally at the end of history (General Judgment). Heaven is the eternal beatitude of union with God. Hell is eternal separation from God. Purgatory, while important, was not traditionally numbered among the Four Last Things as it is transitional.
